market_mood: Risk appetite is strong: tech is at record highs, oil is sliding as Middle East exports normalize, and deal-making is everywhere (McKesson/Option Care, Energy Transfer/Vaquero, Google's 20-year nuclear deal with Constellation).
self_check: My oil and energy calls have been the most reliable (81% right) while rate/bond calls have been choppy, so today I leaned into the oil-price chain and deal news and skipped bond positioning. Low-confidence calls have actually done well, which suggests I should keep sizing conviction honestly rather than crowding everything into 'medium'.

picks.reason: Oil is sliding as Middle East exports rebound to 81% of pre-war levels, which lowers jet fuel costs just as airlines report October earnings, and British Airways' record premium cabin plan underlines the ongoing high-end travel boom United is leveraged to.

McKesson, with CD&R, agreed to a $5.8B takeover of Option Care Health, pushing it deeper into fast-growing home infusion; the target jumped 33% but the acquirer's strategic gain tends to be digested more slowly.
Jamie Dimon warned that new frontier AI systems have raised banks' cyber risk tenfold, the kind of message from a bellwether CEO that tends to lift security budgets over months, not hours.

Energy Transfer is buying Vaquero Midstream for $2.62B in cash and stock, adding Permian gas gathering capacity at a time when power and data-center gas demand is rising; midstream fee income is largely insulated from the falling crude price.

Google's 20-year nuclear supply deal with Constellation sent utility nuclear names soaring; the less-crowded way to play a multi-year nuclear buildout is the equipment and fuel supply chain, which the market connects more slowly.

Crude is slipping as Middle East exports normalize, G7 stockpiles ease supply fears and Saudi pipeline flows rise, yet energy was one of last week's strongest sectors, leaving room to give back gains.

top_buys.pitch: Falling jet fuel plus a premium-travel boom heading into earnings season.
top_buys.why: Gulf oil flows are back to 81% of pre-war rates and crude slipped again today, which directly lowers the biggest variable cost for airlines. British Airways ripping out coach seats for a record 106-seat business cabin shows how strong high-end travel demand is, and United is the US carrier most tilted to premium and international flying. Airline earnings land through October, and fuel relief usually shows up in guidance rather than in the first day's headline.
top_buys.risks: Any renewed Iran escalation could spike crude again, and soft consumer demand would hit bookings even if fuel is cheap.
top_buys.watch: United's Q3 earnings report and commentary on premium cabin demand later in October.

top_buys.pitch: The acquirer in a $5.8B home-infusion deal that the market cheered mostly on the target's side.
top_buys.why: McKesson and CD&R agreed to take Option Care Health private for $5.8B, giving McKesson a much bigger foothold in home infusion, one of the fastest-growing parts of care delivery. Option Care jumped 33% while acquirers typically drift, so the strategic value is digested over weeks. Health care was the weakest sector last week, which makes a company-specific catalyst stand out more.
top_buys.risks: Investors may dislike the capital outlay or worry about integration, and the deal still needs regulatory clearance.
top_buys.watch: Deal terms detail, financing structure and any antitrust commentary in coming weeks.

top_buys.pitch: Dimon says AI just multiplied bank cyber risk tenfold — security budgets follow.
top_buys.why: JPMorgan's CEO publicly warned that powerful new AI systems have escalated financial-sector cyber vulnerability by an order of magnitude, naming cyberattacks the top systemic risk. Warnings like this from the largest US bank typically translate into bigger security spending across financials over quarters. CrowdStrike is a primary beneficiary of enterprise security budget expansion and sits in a strong tech tape.
top_buys.risks: Security stocks are expensive, and any product stumble or competitive pricing pressure could hit the multiple hard.
top_buys.watch: Enterprise security spending commentary and CrowdStrike's next quarterly results.

top_buys.pitch: The picks-and-shovels way to play Google's 20-year nuclear deal after the utilities already spiked.
top_buys.why: Google signed a 20-year nuclear power agreement with Constellation, and Constellation, Vistra and Talen all surged double digits on the day. Chasing those moves is risky, but a multi-decade data-center nuclear buildout needs reactors, components and fuel, which is BWXT's business. That link tends to get repriced days or weeks after the headline rather than instantly.
top_buys.risks: Nuclear supply-chain names are volatile and sentiment-driven; if the AI power trade cools, BWXT falls with it despite no change in fundamentals.
top_buys.watch: Further hyperscaler power deals and BWXT's next order announcements or earnings.

top_buys.pitch: A $2.62B Permian gas acquisition that adds fee income as power demand climbs.
top_buys.why: Energy Transfer agreed to buy Vaquero Midstream in a $2.62B cash-and-stock deal, expanding its natural gas gathering and processing footprint in the Permian. Midstream cash flows are fee-based, so they hold up even as crude prices slip on returning Middle East supply. Rising gas demand from power and data centers gives the added capacity a long runway.
top_buys.risks: Issuing stock for the deal can pressure units near term, and a weak commodity tape could drag the whole energy complex lower.
top_buys.watch: Deal closing timeline and any updated distribution or capex guidance.
